ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: For some 14,000 years hunters, gatherers and fishers lived in settled villages here, and their potters made the world's oldest known ceramics, around 14,500 BCE.
Farming migrants from the Korean Peninsula and the continent brought wet-rice farming, bronze and iron, and mixed with the Jōmon population from about 300 BCE.
Centred around modern Nara, the court from which the imperial line descends built keyhole-shaped burial mounds and received writing and Buddhism through Baekje.
Founded by Emperor Kanmu in 794 on a grid modelled on Chang'an, the capital on the site of modern Kyoto remained the imperial seat for more than a thousand years.
Victor over the Taira in the Genpei War of 1180–1185, Yoritomo set up a warrior government at Kamakura and received the title of shogun in 1192.
Turning against the Kamakura shogunate in 1333, Takauji took Kyoto in 1336 and in 1338 became shogun, founding the Ashikaga, or Muromachi, shogunate.
A warlord of the Sengoku period, Nobunaga began the military unification of Japan that Toyotomi Hideyoshi continued and Tokugawa Ieyasu completed.
After victory at Sekigahara the Tokugawa shoguns ruled from Edo, keeping some 260 daimyo in check through two and a half centuries of internal peace.
Perry's expedition and the unequal treaties undermined the shogunate; in 1868 Emperor Meiji declared power restored, and the domains and the samurai class were abolished.
Born of the Restoration, Japan went from feudal isolation to industrial great power in barely a generation, until a war it could not sustain ended in surrender in 1945.
